text: Neglect of its regulations and inattention to its recommendations, if not outright disobedience to its authority by both individuals and States, soon produced melancholy consequences. These included universal apathy, interstate jealousies and rivalries, the decline of navigation and commerce, and the discouragement of necessary manufacturing. Furthermore, there was a widespread fall in the value of land and its produce, a contempt for public and private faith, a loss of reputation and credit with foreign nations, and, ultimately, growing discontents, animosities, conspiracies, regional conventions, and insurrections that threatened a major national calamity.
